title: A correctness gate asserts a categorical property; only a circuit breaker may carry a threshold
context: SPEC revision 1 proposed a PreToolUse hook denying any Agent dispatch whose brief exceeded 4,000 characters. rules/common/testing.md already forbids that shape: "A pinned count or a sampled allowlist is forbidden — both are change-detectors wearing a census costume." The threshold fails in both directions invisibly: a 3,900-character brief that re-explains the whole conversation passes, and a genuinely self-contained brief carrying an exact SQL block is denied.
options: Keep the 4,000-character gate and tune the number over time
Raise the threshold and accept the false negatives
Forbid thresholds in correctness gates, permitting them only as circuit breakers with a measured basis
outcome: Adopted as SPEC section 0.3 and audited across every mechanism. It removed the brief-length gate and also caught maxTurns, which had passed unexamined as a tuned number. maxTurns survives only as an admitted circuit breaker with values re-derived from measurement: read-only agents observed a legitimate maximum of 115 turns and are set to 300; machinist observed 598 and is set to 800; the runaway that motivated the cap ran 1,184 turns. The three surviving hooks all assert categorical properties — sleep inside a loop, a path matching a task output file, a nesting depth of one.
